Overview

How to use this guide

One set of rules, three ways in. The guide teaches the thinking; the starter kit makes the right answer the easy one in every tool we use.

Every chart we make should do one job: answer a business question so clearly that the reader knows what to do next. The rules here are written to be checked, by a reviewer or by an agent, before a chart leaves the team.

Inspired by the structure of a leading consulting firm's public data-visualization guide, rebuilt for McKesson's brand and for the work of Workforce Innovation.

Consultants and analysts

Decks, reports, workbooks

Read Fundamentals once, then use the chart pages as you build. Keep the cheat sheet next to you.

  • PowerPoint template and starter deck
  • Excel chart workbook with the palette
  • One-page cheat sheet and chart chooser
  • Power BI report theme

Developers and data scientists

Python, HTML, R, Power BI

Each chart page links to tested code. Themes are generated from one token file, so every tool matches.

  • mckviz for matplotlib and Plotly
  • CSS variables, Plotly and Vega-Lite themes
  • theme_mck() for ggplot2
  • mv.lint(fig) to check a chart

Coding agents

Claude, Copilot and others

Agents read AGENTS.md automatically in this repo. For other repos, copy one self-contained rules file.

  • AGENTS.md: workflow and rules
  • mck-chart skill: question to QA
  • dist/agents/mck-viz-rules.md
  • Cookbook pages with runnable snippets

The five steps behind every chart

1 Question. Write the question the chart answers in one sentence.

2 Chart. Pick the chart from the question type, not from habit.

3 Build. Grey first, then color only what the headline names.

4 Headline. Compute the finding, then write it as a sentence.

5 QA. Run the checklist and look at the rendered chart.
